transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what made me come in is that... lately, the things that usually make me feel like myself have started feeling really flat and heavy. 

I normally do things like going on photography walks, mentoring some of the local kids, or even just keeping a really clean, organized calendar. But recently, I just stopped initiating any of it. I'm just not doing the things I usually do, and I wanted to figure out why.
When did you first notice this change in how you were feeling and your motivation to do these activities? Was it a sudden shift or did it develop gradually over time?

It's been about... a year and three months now. I wouldn't say it happened completely overnight, but it definitely started after a family member of mine had some changes in their health and behavior. I had to step in and take on a lot more of the coordination for them—organizing their care and making sure things were handled. Right around that time is when I noticed my own drive for my normal activities just kind of fading out.

Before this year and three months ago when things started changing, have you ever experienced a period like this before—where you lost interest in activities you normally enjoyed and felt that flatness and heaviness for weeks or months at a time?

No, I really haven't. Before all this started with my family member, I was always pretty active and involved. I've never had a time where I just stopped caring about my photography or the mentoring like this. It's completely new for me to feel this... disconnected from everything for so long.

When you're not actively dealing with your family member's care or thinking about their situation, do you still feel that same flatness and heaviness, or does your mood improve when you're distracted from those responsibilities?

Honestly, I haven't really noticed it lifting. Even when I have a quiet evening and I'm not making calls or sorting out their appointments... I don't suddenly feel like going out with my camera or anything. 

The flatness is just kind of always there right now. It doesn't really seem to matter if I'm distracted from the responsibilities or not, it just stays the same.
Besides losing interest in your activities and feeling that flatness, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels over this past year?

Well, my sleep has definitely changed. There have been nights where I only sleep maybe two or three hours. I'll wake up way before dawn, but instead of feeling exhausted, I actually feel completely awake and ready to go. I'll just get up and start answering emails or updating appointment lists for my family member. My energy just feels... different on those nights, like I don't even need the rest. But my appetite has been pretty normal, I think.

During the year and three months since this started, or even before that, have you ever had periods—maybe lasting days or weeks—where you felt unusually energetic, optimistic, or like you could do a lot of things at once, and during those times you needed very little sleep but still felt great rather than tired?

Yeah, that's exactly what happens when my sleep drops off like that. It can go on for a few days at a time where I just have all this drive. 

During those stretches, I just take on everything. I'll start rebuilding my work templates, making detailed care plans, emailing relatives to keep them in the loop, and reorganizing all my files at once. It just feels like... well, like sitting still would mean I'm dropping the ball. So I just keep moving and doing all these things at the same time, and I really don't feel tired while I'm doing it.

When you have those stretches of high energy and little need for sleep where you're doing all these things at once—do those periods feel like they're part of the same overall flatness and heaviness you've been experiencing, or do they feel like a distinctly different state where your mood is actually lifted and more positive?

It definitely feels different from the flatness. Um, during those stretches, I actually feel unusually upbeat. It's like I'm sure everything is just clicking perfectly and I'm on top of it all. 

But... it's not always just positive, I guess. Like, I can be feeling great and getting all this stuff done, and then a tiny change happens—like someone moving a meeting on my calendar at work—and it can make me really sharp with people. It actually surprises me how quick I can snap over something so small during those times. So, yeah, it's a completely different state than the heaviness. I feel really good, but I can get pretty irritable too.

Over this past year and three months, have these stretches of high energy and feeling upbeat been coming and going in a pattern—like they happen for a few days, then you go back to the flatness for a while, then they come back again? Or has it been more random, or something else?

Yeah, they definitely come and go. It's not just a one-time thing. For most of this whole period, I've been cycling back into those driven stretches where I'm overconfident and taking on way too much on practically no sleep. I mean, there are some quieter weeks where I just feel flat and heavy again, but then those high-energy days always seem to come back around. It's been a pretty steady pattern of going back and forth like that.
During those weeks when you're back in the flatness and heaviness, how long do those periods typically last—are we talking about a few days, a week or two, or longer?

Um, the flat periods usually last for a few weeks at a time. I'll have these calm weeks where I'm not all revved up and I'm sleeping normally again. But even during those weeks, I still have other things going on. Like, for more than a couple of weeks at a time during those flat stretches, I'll still hear my name being called when no one is there. And I still get that strong feeling that regular, everyday comments from my boss or coworkers are actually coded tests they're putting me through. So even when the energy and mood drop back down, those other things are still happening.

You mentioned hearing your name being called and feeling like your boss's comments are coded tests—do those things happen during both the high-energy stretches and the flat weeks, or do they mainly happen during one or the other?

They happen during both, actually. But, um, I guess they can feel a bit different depending on how my energy is. 

When I'm in one of those high-energy stretches and running on almost no sleep, the feeling that things are coded gets a lot stronger. Like, if there's a problem with the calendar or an email, I'm just absolutely certain it means something special or it's a test. And during those times, I'll still hear my name being called, or catch those short comments, even when I'm moving a million miles a minute. So yeah, it happens during both the flat weeks and the upbeat ones.

During those flat, heavy weeks when your energy is low and your mood is down, are the feelings about coded messages and hearing your name still happening at the same intensity, or do they fade away during those quieter periods?

They don't fade away, no. Like I was saying, even during those calm weeks when I'm not all revved up and I'm actually sleeping a normal amount, those things are still there. For more than a couple of weeks at a time during those flat stretches, I'll still hear my name being called out of nowhere. And I'll still be completely convinced that ordinary comments from my boss or the people I work with are those coded tests. So, they definitely stick around even when my mood and energy are low.
